title: External Monitor Not Detected
cardText: Diagnose an external monitor that is not detected or displays no image.
Check monitor power, input selection, display cables, Windows settings, USB-C connections and docking stations.
Isolate monitor, cable, graphics driver and computer hardware faults.
text: This guide helps troubleshoot external monitors connected to Windows computers.
Start with monitor power, input selection and cable connections.
Then check Windows display settings, USB-C compatibility, docking stations and graphics drivers.
Test another monitor or computer where possible to identify the faulty component.
Windows instructions are primarily for Windows 11.

checkMonitorPower.title: Check monitor power
body: Confirm the monitor is switched on.
Look for a power indicator light or press the monitor's menu button.
Check whether the monitor displays its own menu, logo or No Signal message.
If the monitor shows no signs of power, check its power cable and outlet.

restoreMonitorPower.title: Restore monitor power
body: Check that the monitor's power cable or adapter is connected securely.
Try a known-working power outlet.
Check the monitor's power button or switch.
If it still shows no signs of power, its power supply or internal hardware may be faulty.
Once the monitor powers on, restart this guide.

checkInputSource.title: Check monitor input source
body: Open the monitor's on-screen menu using its physical buttons or joystick.
Locate Input, Source or Input Select.
Choose the input matching the cable connected to the monitor.
Common inputs include HDMI 1, HDMI 2, DisplayPort, USB-C, DVI and VGA.
Some monitors have several HDMI or DisplayPort inputs, so check the exact socket used.
Wait a few seconds after changing the input.

link.name: Microsoft: Troubleshoot external display connections
link.description: Official guidance covering monitor inputs, cables and display connections.

selectCorrectInput.title: Select the correct monitor input
body: Select the monitor input corresponding to the connected display cable.
Wait for the monitor to detect the computer's video signal.
If the picture appears, the problem was incorrect input selection.
If the monitor remains blank, continue with the cable checks.

checkCableConnection.title: Check display cable connections
body: Disconnect and reconnect the video cable at both the monitor and computer.
Confirm each connector is fully inserted.
Check for damaged connectors, bent pins or loose sockets.
For DisplayPort cables, release any locking mechanism before unplugging.
If using a desktop computer with a dedicated graphics card, check that the monitor is connected to the graphics card rather than an inactive motherboard display output.
Temporarily remove unnecessary adapters or extension cables.

replaceCable.title: Replace the display cable
body: A damaged or unreliable video cable may prevent the monitor from receiving a signal.
Replace the cable with a known-working one of the correct type.
Ensure the replacement supports the required display resolution and refresh rate.
Reconnect the monitor and test again.
If the problem remains, continue with further troubleshooting.

testAnotherCable.title: Test another display cable
body: Try another known-working HDMI, DisplayPort or other suitable cable.
Keep the same monitor and computer ports during the test if possible.
Use a cable that supports the required display mode.
For USB-C connections, the replacement cable must explicitly support video.
If the monitor works with the replacement, the original cable was likely faulty or incompatible.

link.name: Microsoft: External monitor troubleshooting
link.description: Official recommendations for testing replacement display cables.

cableFaultFound.title: Display cable fault identified
body: The monitor works with a different cable.
The original cable was likely faulty or unsuitable for the connection.
Replace it with a compatible cable.
Retest the intended resolution and refresh rate.

testAnotherPort.title: Test another display output
body: If the computer has another compatible display output, try connecting the monitor to it.
Use a known-working cable and select the corresponding input on the monitor.
For desktop computers, prefer outputs on the dedicated graphics card where one is installed.
If changing ports fixes the issue, the original port, its configuration or a compatibility limitation may be responsible.
A different working port does not by itself prove the original port is physically damaged.

displayPortFault.title: Original display output issue
body: The monitor works when connected to a different display output.
The original port may be faulty, disabled or incompatible with the connected device.
Check the computer or graphics card documentation for supported display outputs.
Inspect the original connector for damage.
Use the working output or arrange further diagnostics if necessary.

checkUsbCConnection.title: Is the monitor connected using USB-C?
body: Check whether the display connection uses USB-C directly or through a USB-C adapter.
USB-C ports are not all equivalent.
Some support only USB data or charging and cannot output video.
Select USB-C if the monitor connection uses that connector or an adapter connected to it.
Otherwise continue with Windows display detection.

checkUsbCVideo.title: Check USB-C video compatibility
body: Check the computer's specifications to confirm the USB-C port supports video output.
Look for DisplayPort Alternate Mode, Thunderbolt or USB4 display support.
Ensure any adapter and cable also support the required video connection.
If the computer has multiple USB-C ports, try the one specified for display output.
Some USB-C charging or data cables cannot carry a video signal.
Test using a compatible video-capable cable or adapter before continuing.

link.name: Microsoft: Fix USB-C problems in Windows
link.description: Explains USB-C display compatibility, Alternate Mode and adapter problems.

detectDisplays.title: Detect the monitor in Windows
body: Right-click the Windows desktop and select Display settings.
Alternatively, open Settings, System, Display.
Expand Multiple displays and select Detect.
Wait for Windows to search for an additional monitor.
If the monitor appears, select it and check its display settings.
If Windows reports that no other display was found, continue with connection and driver troubleshooting.

link.name: Microsoft: How to use multiple monitors
link.description: Official instructions for detecting, identifying and arranging multiple displays.

detectDisplays.alt: Windows 11 Display settings showing Multiple displays and Detect other display
detectDisplays.caption: Use Detect in Windows Display settings to search for the connected monitor.

checkDisplayMode.title: Check Windows projection mode
body: Press Windows + P to open the projection menu.
Select Extend to use the monitor as additional desktop space.
Select Duplicate to show the same picture on both screens.
PC screen only disables the external display, while Second screen only disables the computer's primary display.
Choose the appropriate mode and wait for the monitor to respond.
If the monitor remains blank despite being detected, check its resolution and refresh rate.

link.name: Microsoft: Configure multiple monitors
link.description: Explains Duplicate, Extend, PC screen only and Second screen only modes.

checkDisplayMode.alt: Windows 11 projection menu showing PC screen only, Duplicate, Extend and Second screen only
checkDisplayMode.caption: Press Windows + P and choose Extend or Duplicate as appropriate.

checkResolution.title: Check resolution and refresh rate
body: Open Settings, System, Display.
Select the external monitor from the display diagram.
Choose a resolution supported by the monitor, preferably the recommended resolution.
Open Advanced display and check the refresh rate.
If the monitor remains blank, try a common supported refresh rate such as 60 Hz where available.
High resolutions and refresh rates require compatible graphics hardware, cables, adapters and docks.
Allow Windows to revert any unsupported display mode if the picture disappears.

link.name: Microsoft: Multiple monitor settings
link.description: Official guidance for changing display resolution, refresh rate and display layout.

checkDockingStation.title: Check docking station or display adapter
body: Determine whether the monitor connects through a docking station, USB-C hub or video adapter.
A dock may require its own power supply, drivers or firmware.
Check that the dock supports the computer and the monitor's required resolution and refresh rate.
Some USB-C docks require a USB-C port with DisplayPort Alternate Mode or Thunderbolt support.
If no dock or adapter is being used, continue with graphics driver troubleshooting.

link.name: Microsoft: External monitor troubleshooting
link.description: Includes recommendations for troubleshooting docks, adapters and display connections.

testWithoutDock.title: Test the monitor without the dock
body: If the computer has a suitable display output, connect the monitor directly to it.
Use a compatible cable and select the correct monitor input.
This test helps isolate problems caused by the dock or adapter.
If the monitor works directly, check the dock's power supply, firmware, driver and supported display limits.
If the monitor still fails when connected directly, continue troubleshooting the computer.

dockFaultFound.title: Dock or adapter issue identified
body: The monitor works when connected directly to the computer.
The docking station, hub or adapter may be incompatible, misconfigured or faulty.
Check that the dock has sufficient power and supports the required video outputs.
Install manufacturer-recommended dock firmware and drivers where appropriate.
Check maximum supported monitor counts, resolutions and refresh rates.
Replace or repair the dock if it still fails.

checkGraphicsDriver.title: Check the graphics driver
body: If Windows is responding, press Windows + Ctrl + Shift + B to reset the graphics driver.
The screen may briefly flash or go blank during the reset.
Restart the computer and test the external monitor again.
Open Device Manager and expand Display adapters.
Check for warning symbols or device errors.
Install a compatible graphics driver from the computer or graphics card manufacturer if necessary.
If the problem began immediately after a graphics driver update, consider using Roll Back Driver in Device Manager.

link.name: Microsoft: Troubleshoot external monitors
link.description: Official instructions for resetting, updating, reinstalling and rolling back display drivers.

testAnotherMonitor.title: Test another monitor or computer
body: Connect another known-working monitor or TV to the computer.
Use a suitable known-working cable and the same computer output if possible.
Also test the original monitor on another computer where practical.
If the replacement monitor works but the original does not, investigate the original monitor's settings, input or hardware.
If several known-working monitors fail on the computer, the computer's display output or software is more likely to be responsible.

monitorFault.title: Original monitor or compatibility issue likely
body: A different monitor works with the same computer.
Test the original monitor with another computer and a known-working cable.
Check the original monitor's input source and supported resolutions.
Try restoring the monitor's default settings using its on-screen menu if appropriate.
If the monitor fails on multiple computers, a hardware fault is likely.
Arrange repair or replacement if necessary.

hardwareEscalation.title: Further graphics hardware diagnostics required
body: Multiple known-working monitors fail after checking cables, ports, Windows settings, docks and graphics drivers.
Possible causes include graphics hardware faults, damaged display outputs, USB-C controller problems or system firmware issues.
Check whether the graphics hardware supports the number of connected monitors and their required resolutions.
For desktop computers, confirm external displays are connected to the intended graphics outputs.
Review the computer manufacturer's BIOS, firmware and graphics driver guidance.
Record the computer model, monitor model, connection type and troubleshooting results before arranging further diagnostics.

link.name: Microsoft: External monitor troubleshooting
link.description: Official reference for unresolved display connection and graphics driver problems.
